issues.detail: Six of Grokbot's 7 tab_items are process text or boilerplate, not requirements: 'Using the Checklist Please include a completed checklist...'; the '28 days to provide the required information' invalid-application process; 'Two hard copies and 2 CDs for major applications' (repeated three times, with page/section number fragments '4 Full Planning Applications', '7 Outline...', '10 Reserved Matters...' run into it); 'Any confidential data should be sent separately'; and the redacted-copy note. Only the Financial Viability Assessment item is a real requirement, and it was filed under 'Submission rules' with no trigger. The reference row claims 30 requirement items, but the tab holds 7.
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'Any confidential data should be sent separately clearly stating its confidentiality. 7 Outline Planning Application (Major and Minor) Two hard copies and 2 CDs for major applications.'

issues.detail: Several rows are filed under the wrong application type because Grokbot took text from a neighbouring checklist section. Under Householder, 'Telecommunications supplementary information' (ICNIRP declaration, details of consultation) and 'CIL Additional Information / Form' come from the prior approval (telecoms/non-householder) sections, and 'Floor plans / Elevations' are national requirements from the same telecoms prior approval block. Under 'Change of use - prior approval', 'Telecommunications supplementary information' and 'Block plan' come from the telecoms prior approval section, and 'Flood Risk Assessment' is the general FRA definition, not a prior approval requirement. Under 'Permission in principle', 'Arboricultural Impact Assessment / Tree Survey' and 'Photographs' are the local requirements of the section before '27 Permission in Principle' (the tree works section), not PiP. 'Works to trees' is still marked '(none)'.
issues.evidence: trigger_excerpt: 'Local Requirement ❏ Tree Survey - when felling ❏ Photographs Note: Any confidential data ... 27 Permission in Principle National Requirement ❏ Completed application form ❏ Planning Statement'

issues.detail: About 20 rows from the 'Definitions' section were put under Full planning with the note 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. Examples: Air Quality, Ecology, EIA, Accessibility Statement, Basement Impact Assessment, Heritage Statement, TVIA, Tall Building Assessment, Transport, Travel Plan. The checklist is set out per application type, each with its own 'Local Requirement' checkboxes, so where each item applies should come from those per-type boxes, not from a guess. Some of these items (e.g. heritage statement, basement assessment) would also apply to householder, listed building or outline applications.
issues.evidence: notes on rows: 'INFERRED: application type not named in extracted text of a general local list; placed under Full planning - check source for applicability'

issues.detail: Outline, Reserved matters, Listed building consent, Advertisement consent, Lawful development certificate, Demolition in a conservation area, s73, Discharge of conditions, Non-material amendment and Works to trees are all marked '(none)', yet the checklist has a numbered section for each type with 'Local Requirement' boxes. Grokbot's own extract shows section headings such as '7 Outline Planning Application', '10 Reserved Matters Application' and the tree works section ('Tree Survey - when felling', 'Photographs'). The specific local items per type could not be listed because the source could not be fetched this run.
issues.evidence: tab_items/trigger_excerpts reference sections 4, 7, 10, 18, 19, 27 and 28 of the checklist; app_type_rows show '(none)' for 10 of these types
issues.grok_comment: Right for Outline, RM, LBC, adverts, LDC, discharge, NMA and tree works, which all have sections with Local Requirement boxes. But the Feb 2024 checklist has no s73 or demolition-in-conservation-area section (only 'Prior notification (demolitions)').
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. s73 and demolition in a conservation area are withdrawn (no such sections). The other types stand.

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are raw checkbox text that runs across section boundaries, or fragments that give no trigger. 'CIL Additional Information / Form' runs into '19 Prior Approval (Non-Householder) National Requirement...'. 'Planning Statement' runs into '28 Definitions ... Accessibility Statement'. 'Landscaping scheme' is just 'the proposed landscaping scheme.' 'Lighting Assessment' begins mid-sentence with 'watercourse where external lighting...'. 'Design and Access Statement' is 'The statement can be incorporated into design and access statements where these are required.', which comes from a different item's definition. 'Retail Impact' begins mid-sentence. None of these state when the requirement applies.
issues.evidence: Design and Access Statement trigger_excerpt: 'The statement can be incorporated into design and access statements where these are required.'

issues.detail: Some requirement names do not match the text mapped to them. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' is mapped to construction/demolition method statement text (traffic, dust, noise, vibration). 'Marketing / vacancy evidence (loss of use)' is mapped to the retail impact assessment trigger. 'Ventilation / Extraction details (odour)' and 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage details' are both mapped to noise assessment text about plant and glass collection.
issues.evidence: Waste row trigger_excerpt: 'details of waste collection for example pubs/clubs where glass collection could be noisy.'

issues.detail: Several rows share the same excerpt and are counted as separate requirements: 'Transport Assessment' and 'Travel Plan' (both the travel plan text); 'Ground investigation / Basement Impact Assessment' and 'Structural Survey' (both the BIA text); 'Arboricultural/Tree Survey', 'Photographs' and 'Planning Statement', which repeat under both Full planning and PiP.
issues.evidence: Both rows: 'Basement Impact Assessment/Structural Survey Where a proposed development includes a new or extended basement...'

summary: Grokbot's Hillingdon row probably points to an older copy (or an old URL variant) of a checklist the council now titles 'February 2024', and it dates the list June 2020 from the URL. Its extraction is mostly boilerplate, with garbled cross-section triggers and requirements filed under the wrong application types. Live reading was not possible because the shared WebFetch and WebSearch budgets ran out, so the findings rest on search-index evidence and inspection of Grokbot's own extract.

withdrawn_issues.detail: No Biodiversity Net Gain requirement appears anywhere in Grokbot's rows. The revision indexed as February 2024 lines up with mandatory BNG starting on 12 Feb 2024, so it may add BNG and other changes that a 2020-based extraction would miss. Needs checking against the February 2024 text.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: No BNG row in app_type_rows; current version titled February 2024 (search index)
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The source checked (the 'February 2024' checklist) has no BNG or 'net gain' wording at all; 'biodiversity' appears only once, in the construction method statement text. So no BNG row is a correct capture, not a missed requirement.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The checklist has no BNG wording, so no BNG row is a correct capture. (Statutory BNG is national anyway.)
